::: {.why}
The fundamental law is the arithmetic every quant interview expects you to produce on demand, and the gap you found last night between it and your measured Sharpe is where its assumptions failed.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the relationship between information ratio, IC and breadth and name the assumptions behind it.
- Explain the discrepancy between the law's prediction and your engine's measured Sharpe for one signal.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Derive the relationship rather than quoting it: for N independent bets with forecast-outcome correlation IC, the annualised information ratio is approximately IC times the square root of the number of bets per year. Do the derivation and note precisely where independence enters.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Diagnose the gap for your signal, which will come from some combination of four things: the bets are not independent because names are correlated, the transfer coefficient is below one because constraints stop you holding the ideal portfolio, costs are not in the law, and the IC estimate itself is noisy. Estimate the size of each of the four for your signal and check they account for the discrepancy.
:::
:::
